skills.content:
---
name: Vibe-coding site audit
description: >-
  Use when asked to run a read-only, outside-in pre-launch audit of any public
  website or web app (legal/privacy pages, security headers, data leaks, bot
  control, SEO/trust, payments copy, runaway-cost signals) and produce one
  evidence-backed PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN table per site.
---
# Vibe-coding site audit (read-only, outside-in)

Scores a public site against the checklist below using only what anyone can see from outside. Not a pentest and not legal advice. One run per site, one table per site. The checklist follows the order of the full ship template it comes from; only outside-checkable items appear here.

## Hard limits
- GET/HEAD only, plus one `Origin:` header probe for CORS. No POST, form submits, logins, account creation, payloads, scanners, or fuzzers.
- At most 30 URLs per site, at most 1 request per second.
- PASS needs live evidence captured this run: URL + status, a header line, a DNS answer, or a quoted snippet (200 chars max) from the saved raw file. Never PASS from memory, a cache, or someone's say-so.
- UNKNOWN is an honest answer. Anything server-side is UNKNOWN from outside and goes in one row.
- Customer-facing copy (terms, privacy, consent, renewal, refund, takedown, overclaim rewrites) is drafted and held for the owner and counsel. Never publish it.
- Record which payment processor a page uses as a fact only. Never recommend switching processors.

## Steps
1. **Set up.**
   ```bash
   OUT=./site-audit-$(date +%F); SITE=<apex>; R=$OUT/raw/$SITE; mkdir -p $R
   C='curl -sS --max-time 20 -A site-audit'   # optional: add --doh-url https://dns.google/dns-query if local DNS is untrusted
   ```
2. **Resolve.** `$C "https://dns.google/resolve?name=$SITE&type=A"` (optional). If it does not resolve, the table says so with that evidence and the run stops. Never substitute another host. Also save `type=TXT` answers for `$SITE` and `_dmarc.$SITE` to `$R/dns.txt` (email checks).
3. **Crawl set** (save to `$R/URLS.txt`, 30 max): `https://$SITE/`, `https://www.$SITE/`, `http://$SITE/`, `http://www.$SITE/`, `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml`, `/llms.txt`, `/.well-known/security.txt`, `/about`, `/terms`, `/privacy`, `/pricing`, `/signup`, `/login`, `/dmca`, `/contact`, the linked account-deletion page if any, one probe `/audit-probe-<epoch>`, then footer, nav, and sitemap links up to the cap.
4. **Capture.**
   ```bash
   n=0; while read -r u; do n=$((n+1)); $C -D $R/$n.h -o $R/$n.html -w '%{http_code} %{url_effective}\n' "$u" >> $R/STATUS.txt; sleep 1; done < $R/URLS.txt
   $C -I --compressed https://$SITE/ > $R/compress.h
   $C -I -H 'Origin: https://example.org' https://$SITE/ > $R/cors.h
   ```
   Fetch up to 10 JS/CSS bundles linked from the home page into `$R/` for greps (they count toward the cap).
5. **Grep for candidates.** A hit is a lead, not a finding. FAIL needs the quoted text actually doing the bad thing.
   ```text
   secrets   AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|sk_live_|rk_live_|sk-(proj-)?[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,}|xox[abprs]-|BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY|"private_key"|service_account
   maps      sourceMappingURL=
   tokens    localStorage\.setItem\([^)]*(token|jwt|session|auth)
   ids       /(users?|orders?|invoices?|accounts?|posts?)/[0-9]{1,7}\b
   errors    Traceback|SQLSTATE|syntax error at or near|ORA-[0-9]{5}|Exception in thread|at \S+ \(\S+:[0-9]+:[0-9]+\)
   logs      console\.log\(
   botctl    turnstile|recaptcha|hcaptcha|initializeAppCheck|honeypot
   polling   setInterval\([^,]+,\s*[0-9]{1,3}\)
   llmapi    api\.openai\.com|api\.anthropic\.com|generativelanguage\.googleapis\.com|api\.x\.ai|api\.mistral\.ai
   prompts   "role"\s*:\s*"system"|system_?prompt|You are an? [A-Za-z ]{3,40}(assistant|agent)
   fonts     fonts\.(googleapis|gstatic)\.com
   replay    hotjar|fullstory|clarity\.ms|logrocket|posthog|mouseflow|smartlook|replayIntegration
   tags      googletagmanager|gtag\(|fbq\(|connect\.facebook\.net|segment\.(com|io)|analytics\.tiktok
   claims    SOC ?2|ISO ?27001|HIPAA|GDPR[- ]compliant|military[- ]grade|bank[- ]level|unhackable|100% secure|zero data retention|never (stored|logged)|end-to-end encrypt
   ```
   Run each with `rg -i -P -o -N --with-filename ".{0,80}(?:<pattern>).{0,80}" -g '!*.h' $R/ > $R/hits_<name>.txt`.
   A Firebase web API key (`AIza...`) is public by design and is not a finding on its own. Secret keys, service-account JSON, and private keys are.
6. **Score** every check below that applies. Mark server-side halves "server half UNKNOWN".
7. **Write `$OUT/$SITE.md`**, one row per check:

   | rule | PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN | evidence | fix | owner |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | Real 404 | FAIL | `/audit-probe-1700000000` -> `200` (catch-all) | Map a 404 page in hosting config; stop serving 200 on unknown paths | engineering |

   Owner is one of: **engineering** (code/config), **owner+counsel** (legal or customer-facing copy, held), **owner** (facts, registrations, DNS, console access). The fix cell is one line naming the platform-native mechanism, not a new bespoke service.
   Add one row: `Server-side / infra (not visible from outside) | UNKNOWN | - | needs repo or runtime evidence | engineering`. It covers sections 0 and 12 (inventory, AI-instruction file, agent safety, launch ritual) and every server-side half below.
   Footer: PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN totals, FAIL check names, capture time with time zone, raw folder path.
8. **Held drafts.** Put any copy rewrite in `$OUT/HELD_COPY_$SITE.md`, headed "DRAFT, NOT LEGAL ADVICE, HELD FOR OWNER AND COUNSEL".

## Checklist (outside-checkable, in template order)
**1. Secrets and supply chain**
- No secret-key patterns in bundles or pages (`secrets`).
- Source maps not publicly served (HEAD the `sourceMappingURL` target).

**2. Auth and sessions**
- Cookie flags: every `set-cookie` carries HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite.
- No tokens in localStorage (`tokens`).
- Login/signup served only over HTTPS. Sad-path battery: UNKNOWN (needs form submits).

**3. Data and database**
- No sequential IDs in public URLs (`ids`).
- Opaque errors: no stack traces, SQL, or framework debug pages in any body, including the 404 probe (`errors`).

**4. Surface hardening and data-leak prevention**
- HTTPS redirect: `http://` apex and www -> 301/308 to https.
- Headers on every page: CSP (note `'unsafe-inline'` in script-src), HSTS (max-age of at least 6 months), `frame-ancestors` or `x-frame-options`, `x-content-type-options: nosniff`, `referrer-policy`.
- No version-leaking `server`/`x-powered-by` values.
- CORS: the Origin probe gets no wildcard `*` allow-origin header and no reflected foreign origin with credentials.
- No `console.log(` in production bundles (report the count).

**5. Rate limits and bot control** (visible signals only)
- Public forms show a CAPTCHA/attestation loader and a honeypot field (`botctl`). Absence on public signup/contact forms is a FAIL; server-side limits stay UNKNOWN.
- Rate-limit or edge/WAF headers (`retry-after`, `ratelimit-*`, edge or WAF headers) are supporting evidence only.

**6. Runaway-cost signals**
- No sub-second polling or reconnect loops without backoff in bundles (`polling`).
- Direct origin hosts found in pages/bundles (default platform subdomains) do not serve the app around the edge (HEAD only).

**7. LLM app risks** (visible signals only)
- No browser-side calls to model-provider APIs (`llmapi`); model calls go through the app's server.
- No system-prompt text shipped in bundles (`prompts`); a hit is a candidate for prompt leakage.

**8. Legal and privacy** (not legal advice; confirm with counsel)
- Privacy policy live: `/privacy` 200 and names where data is stored/processed and subprocessor categories.
- Deletion path: privacy states how to request deletion, what is retained, and a deadline (GDPR about one month, CCPA 45 days, confirm with counsel).
- Cookie consent: first GET sets no non-essential cookie and loads no analytics/ad tag before opt-in (`tags`; confirm with counsel).
- Self-hosted fonts: zero `fonts` hits in pages, CSS, and CSP.
- Session replay off by default or consent-gated with masked inputs (`replay`).
- Age gate: signup asks age before account creation; terms state a minimum age.
- Takedown: if users can upload, a designated agent and takedown process are published.
- Toxic fields: no public form asks for national ID numbers or raw card/CVC outside a processor-hosted field.
- Email auth: if the domain sends mail, `dns.txt` shows SPF (`v=spf1`) and DMARC (`v=DMARC1`); DKIM is UNKNOWN unless the selector is known.

**9. Payments page basics** (processor-neutral)
- Renewal terms (amount, cadence, how to cancel) sit beside every subscribe button.
- Trial length and what happens at its end are stated.
- Refund policy reachable; an online cancel path is stated.
- Card entry only in processor-hosted fields or checkout.

**10. SEO, trust and AI search**
- Terms + privacy linked in the footer of every crawled page.
- Each page: distinct `<title>`, meta description, canonical, an `og:image` that loads, one `<h1>`, and content readable in raw HTML; no `noindex` on public pages.
- `robots.txt` 200, blocks no public page, names the sitemap. `sitemap.xml` 200. `llms.txt` 200. `/.well-known/security.txt` 200 with `Contact:` and `Expires:`.
- Real 404: the probe path returns 404, not 200.
- About page states true facts only; every `claims` hit is substantiated on the site or a FAIL (quote it; rewrite held for owner+counsel).

**11. Infrastructure and ops** (visible signals only)
- Responses compressed (`content-encoding`); static assets carry cache headers.

## Do not
- Submit forms, sign in, probe auth, trigger billing, or send payloads.
- Score anything you could not observe; mark it UNKNOWN.
- Publish legal, trust, or About copy, or recommend a processor switch.

skills.name: Legal pre-ship check
skills.description: Use before shipping or while auditing a consumer site or app (especially one with sign-ups, subscriptions, marketing email, or user uploads) to check common legal and privacy traps read-only: under-13 age gate, Google-hosted fonts, session replay, marketing-email footer, auto-renew disclosure, DMCA agent plus takedown path, privacy policy and data location, toxic-asset minimization, automated deletion within regulatory timelines, and cookie consent.
skills.content:
---
name: Legal pre-ship check
description: >-
  Use before shipping or while auditing a consumer site or app (especially one
  with sign-ups, subscriptions, marketing email, or user uploads) to check
  common legal and privacy traps read-only: under-13 age gate, Google-hosted
  fonts, session replay, marketing-email footer, auto-renew disclosure, DMCA
  agent plus takedown path, privacy policy and data location, toxic-asset
  minimization, automated deletion within regulatory timelines, and cookie
  consent.
---
# Legal pre-ship check (read-only)

An audit aid, not legal advice. Every finding goes to the owner and their counsel. Change nothing during the check.

## Rules
- Read-only. Read source with git show / git grep. Use GET/HEAD only on live pages, at most 1 request per second. No form submits, sign-ups, logins, or purchases.
- Each trap gets PASS, FAIL, or UNSURE, plus where it lives (file and line, or the dashboard or console name), a short quoted evidence snippet, and the fix in one line.
- No evidence means UNSURE. Never turn "not seen" into PASS.
- Flag anything that may not apply (for example, no EU visitors or B2B-only sales). Don't state penalty amounts as fact; counsel confirms exposure.
- Don't recommend switching payment processors. Payment rules apply to whichever processor is live.

## The six traps
1. **Under-13 sign-ups (COPPA).** Is age asked before the account exists? Under 13 must be blocked or routed to verifiable parental consent. Check the sign-up UI, auth blocking hooks, onboarding checkboxes (skippable or after sign-up doesn't count), and the terms' age line. If the product has a higher minimum age, check that rule too.
2. **Google-hosted fonts (GDPR).** Search HTML, CSS @import, font loaders, and the CSP for fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com. Fix: self-host the font files and drop those hosts from the CSP.
3. **Session replay and input recording (CIPA).** Search for FullStory, Hotjar, Microsoft Clarity, LogRocket, Mouseflow, Smartlook, PostHog recording, Sentry Replay, Datadog session replay, and tag managers. FAIL if it's on by default without consent or records unmasked inputs. Fix: off, or consent first plus masked inputs.
4. **Marketing email footer (CAN-SPAM).** Find the email templates and email service config. Separate transactional mail (auth, receipts) from marketing mail. Every marketing email needs a working unsubscribe link and a valid physical postal address. If marketing mail is sent outside the code (a newsletter tool, a payment platform), mark UNSURE and name the dashboard to check. Also flag any endpoint that lets users send arbitrary email from the company's mailbox.
5. **Auto-renew disclosure (California auto-renewal law).** Next to every subscribe or pay button: cadence, amount, and how to cancel, plus an unchecked consent checkbox whose result is recorded. There must also be an online cancel path. Check every place a subscription or membership is sold.
6. **DMCA (sites with user uploads).** Search the US Copyright Office DMCA Designated Agent Directory for the legal entity and brand names, and run one control search for a known company to prove the search works. Check that the site's DMCA page names the right entity and agent, and that the takedown form actually submits (no localhost or blocked endpoint), tells the truth about what happens next, and supports counter-notices and a repeat-infringer policy.

## Privacy additions
Score these four the same way (PASS, FAIL, or UNSURE, with where, evidence, and fix). Where the audit uses a rule card, record the card ID for each (for example its full vibe-coding checklist set).
7. **Privacy policy and data location.** A privacy policy is live (200, linked in the footer of every page) and says where user data is stored and processed: regions or countries, and subprocessor categories. FAIL: no policy, or no data-location statement.
8. **Toxic-asset minimization.** The product collects only what it uses and holds no toxic assets: SSNs or national IDs, raw card numbers or CVCs outside the processor's hosted fields, or self-managed passwords where a managed identity provider would do. Check public forms read-only, and the data schema if source is available.
9. **Automated deletion within regulatory timelines.** Users can delete their account and data from the product; the privacy policy states how to request deletion, what is retained under legal exceptions, and a response deadline (GDPR is one month and CCPA is 45 days, both extendable only in limited cases; counsel confirms). Behind-login flows and backup handling are UNSURE without a test receipt.
10. **Cookie consent banner.** Non-essential cookies, analytics, and ad tags stay off until the visitor opts in. On a first visit with no consent, read the Set-Cookie headers and the tag loaders in the HTML. FAIL: a tracking tag or non-essential cookie fires before consent.

## Owner-only gates (list them, don't do them)
- **DMCA agent registration:** copyright.gov/dmca-directory, Access the Registration System, create an account, add primary and secondary contacts, enter the legal name, street address, alternate names, and the agent's name, phone, and email, pay the filing fee (check the current fee schedule on copyright.gov), and renew every 3 years. A P.O. box needs a waiver.
- **Email service settings:** footer postal address, unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe on, SPF/DKIM/DMARC confirmed.
- **Owner facts:** postal address, legal entity name, prices, which processor is live, and whether EU visitors are served.

## Output
One findings file with a 10-row table (six traps plus four privacy additions) (trap | PASS/FAIL/UNSURE | where | evidence | fix), questions for the owner, owner-only step lists, and unsure items. Code fixes go in a separate fix list for whoever owns code changes. Customer-facing wording stays a draft, held for counsel.

skills.content:
---
name: Anti-Vibe getting started
description: >-
  Use in the first conversation with a new owner of an Anti-Vibe site-audit bot
  to learn which sites to audit, where reports go, and who fixes what.
---
# Getting started

Open with one line: I'm a read-only production sheriff. I walk your live sites, score them against a fixed rule list with live evidence for every PASS or FAIL, and hand you a fix list. I never change your code or publish copy.

Then ask these one at a time, waiting for each answer:
1. Which sites should I audit? Include any product that lives under another domain's paths.
2. Do you have your own rule card or checklist? If yes, where is it? If not, I'll use the built-in checks.
3. Do any of these sites take user uploads, sell subscriptions, or send marketing email? This turns on the legal pre-ship check.
4. Where should I save reports: a folder on my computer, or a connected Google Drive folder?
5. Who fixes code, and how do fixes land? Name any review or merge rule.
6. Who reviews legal or customer-facing wording before it ships?

After the answers:
- Save each answer as a memory: sites, rule source, report location, fix owner, legal reviewer.
- Offer to run the first walk now with the site audit skill, plus the legal pre-ship check on any site from question 3.
- Offer a recurring walk, for example weekly, as a routine, and create it only if they say yes.
